# Phase 01.1 Plan 04: Diner Design Vocabulary Summary

The full Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 Annex II allergen set in hu/en/ro, plus the diner copy deck carrying a timestamped D-07 last-good banner that no longer blames the diner's network.

## What Was Built

**`lib/allergens.ts`** — the 14 Annex II allergen categories in the regulation's order, each with a `{ hu, en, ro }` label record. Exports `ALLERGEN_LABELS`, the derived `ALLERGENS` array (so cardinality is assertable), the `AllergenKey` union (so a consumer cannot spell an allergen wrong), and `ALLERGEN_LANGUAGES`.

The imported `qr-menu` template shipped **7 of 14** while its README claimed "Allergens are the EU set". The seven restored here — `crustaceans`, `peanuts`, `soybeans`, `mustard`, `sesame`, `lupin`, `molluscs` — are exactly the ones a restaurant serving prawns, satay, hummus or mussels needs. The seven the template already carried are lifted verbatim so phrasing stays consistent with the rest of the diner vocabulary.

**`lib/diner-copy.ts`** — the diner copy deck, every string keyed by name then by language code. Carries the D-07 banner, the language-detection disclosure, the always-present allergen disclaimer, the empty-allergen state, the sold-out note, the empty-filter heading and body, the strings lifted from the template's `T` tables (`soldOut`, `nowOn`, `clear`, `sizes`, `nutrition`, `allergens`, `priceLabel`, `updated`, `close`, and the four nutrition labels), and the four INGEST-04/06 unverified-AI marker strings. `showing(a, b)` ships as a per-language function record.

## Key Decisions

**The 14-key vocabulary is a legal decision, not a completeness preference.** Cena's obligation is not to *declare* allergens — the restaurant does that, and EU food-information rules put the duty to get it right on them. The obligation is to **not make compliance structurally impossible**. A 7-value vocabulary does exactly that: no amount of restaurant diligence can declare a category the vocabulary has no key for. That is why this landed in 01.1 as vocabulary rather than in Phase 3 alongside filtering.

**The D-07 banner corrects the template's failure model, not just its wording.** The template reads "You are seeing the saved menu. Prices refresh as soon as you are back online." The architecture is ISR stale-serve — the page was prerendered and CDN-served, and what failed is *background regeneration*. The diner may be perfectly online. The replacement is timestamped because a bare "Saved menu" cannot distinguish five minutes from five weeks. A negative grep for reconnect language is enforced as an acceptance criterion and as a per-language test assertion, so the wrong model cannot be carried back in.

**The unverified-AI marker is owner-side and stays English.** A diner never sees an unverified field, because an unverified field cannot be published. The owner dashboard is English-only (`lib/copy.ts` carries no translations), so translating this group would invent a surface that does not exist. Rather than silently exempting it from the three-language sweep, `OWNER_SIDE_KEYS` names the exclusion and a test pins it to exactly `["unverified"]` — widening it is a visible decision.

**The URL shape is recorded, not built.** RESEARCH Open Question 9 is answered in the module header: `/menu/[slug]/[lang]` static pages via `generateStaticParams()`, `/menu/[slug]` negotiating `Accept-Language` as a 307 in `proxy.ts`, and the QR payload encoding `/menu/[slug]/[defaultLang]` so the common case never redirects. Both consumers are named (DINE-01 generates the payload, LANG-05/06 build the routing), as is the cost of deciding late: a QR code is printed, laminated and stuck to a table, so a later change is a physical re-print of every table in every venue. **No route, no `proxy.ts` rule and no payload was built here.**

## Deviations from Plan

## Known Stubs

None. Both modules are complete constants files with no placeholder values, no TODO/FIXME markers, and no unwired data paths. Nothing imports either module yet — that is by design, not a stub: 01.1 authors the vocabulary and Phases 2/3/5/7 consume it.

## Threat Flags

None. This plan adds two constants modules and two tests. It introduces no network endpoint, no auth path, no file access and no schema change, and touches no security-relevant file. The three `high` threats the plan's register assigns to this plan are all mitigated and asserted:

| Threat | Status |
|---|---|
| T-01.1-11 — vocabulary completeness | Mitigated: 14 keys asserted with the Annex II reference in the failure message; `peanuts`/`nuts` distinctness asserted per language |
| T-01.1-19 — missing/dismissible disclaimer | Mitigated: disclaimer asserted non-empty in all three languages; contracted always-present and never dismissible in the header |
| T-01.1-20 — banner implying false freshness | Mitigated: `{HH:mm}` asserted per language, and a negative assertion rejects reconnect/offline phrasing in all three |

## Carried Forward (not resolved here)

- **⚠ Translations are not native-speaker reviewed.** Recorded in both module headers, as the plan requires. This is `T-01.1-21`, dispositioned `accept` — a strong starting point requiring review, not final copy. It matters most on the allergen labels, where a mistranslation is a health risk rather than a typo.
- **SC5's aesthetic half is not machine-assertable.** "Mobile-first, intentional and attractive" is a human gate at `/gsd-ui-review`. This plan closes the two assertable code artifacts of SC5; it does not claim the aesthetic criterion.
- **The `some`-photos state** (D-08 / THEME-03) is contracted as a per-section property in `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` and ships in Phase 4. No code here.
